prompt_md: A hen and a half lays an egg and a half in a day and a half. At that rate, how many eggs does one hen lay in 3 days?
prompt_short: A hen and a half, an egg and a half, a day and a half. One hen, 3 days?
hint_md: First find how long one hen takes for one egg.
explain_intuition_md: Fewer hens means fewer eggs in the same time: one hen lays one egg in a day and a half. Three days is two of those stretches, so two eggs.
explain_math_md: $\frac{1.5 \text{ eggs}}{1.5 \text{ hens} \times 1.5 \text{ days}} = \frac{2}{3}$ egg per hen-day, $\times 3 = 2$.
